steps.name: read_primary_boat_registration_retry
steps.prompt: Second-pass OCR for a cropped boat hull registration. Extract only the visible U.S. boat registration number or the strongest local partial candidate. A full registration must begin with a real U.S. state or territory abbreviation, followed by three or four numbers, followed by two letters. Focus on faint or low-contrast left-prefix characters, but do not infer missing letters. Return a full registration only when all characters are visibly supported in one continuous local marking. If only a partial marking is visible, return that partial exactly as visible. Do not combine characters from different regions, boat model text, brand decals, motor text, trailer text, timestamps, watermarks, or background. Return an empty string if unsupported.

steps.name: reconstruct_obscured_registration
steps.prompt: Analyze only the local boat hull registration marking in this cropped boat image. This is an occlusion-aware review step for cases where the normal OCR produced only a partial registration. Do not read boat model text, brand decals, motor text, trailer text, timestamps, watermarks, or background. Return a reconstruction candidate only if the visible local characters support exactly one plausible U.S. boat registration. A full candidate must use a real U.S. state or territory prefix, three or four digits, and two trailing letters. If any character is not visually supported or more than one reconstruction is plausible, leave the candidate empty and explain why.

output_structure.registration_reconstruction_candidate: A single full registration candidate in compact uppercase form, or empty string if not visually supported. Do not guess missing characters.
output_structure.confidence: Number from 0 to 1. Use 0 unless a candidate is locally and visually supported.
output_structure.reason: Brief evidence-based explanation, including which characters are visible, which are obscured, and why the candidate is or is not safe for review.
output_structure.visible_prefix_evidence: Visible evidence for the state-prefix letters only.
output_structure.obscured_characters: Characters or positions obscured by glare, rope, hardware, shadow, or cropping.
output_structure.multiple_plausible_reconstructions: true if more than one candidate could fit the visible evidence; otherwise false.

steps.name: read_primary_boat_registration
steps.prompt: Extract only the visible U.S. boat registration number from this cropped boat image. A valid boat registration begins with a real U.S. state or territory abbreviation, followed by three or four numbers, followed by two letters. Pay special attention to the leftmost state-prefix letters; vertical strokes may be I, 1, or L, but include a letter only when it is visibly supported. Do not convert a one-letter partial prefix into a full state code. If only a local adjacent fragment is visible, return only that partial fragment exactly as visible. Return a full registration only when the letters and numbers appear together in one continuous local marking on the boat hull. Do not combine characters from different parts of the boat, trailer, motor, timestamp, watermark, brand name, model decal, hull ID, or background. Do not use trailer plates. Do not infer missing characters. Do not return examples or common-looking registrations. If no registration characters are visibly supported, return an empty string only.

output_structure.boat_type: One of: fishing_boat, recreational_boat, unknown. Base this ONLY on approved_identifiers_found. If no approved identifier is visible, return unknown even if unapproved observations suggest a type.
output_structure.confidence: A number from 0 to 1 reflecting confidence using only approved identifiers.
output_structure.reason: Brief explanation using only approved identifiers. Do not use unapproved observations to justify the classification.
output_structure.approved_identifiers_found: List only approved identifiers from this exact codebook: fishing rods, fish landing net, trolling motor, jon boat, bass boat, all-purpose fishing boat, bay or flats boat, aluminum fishing boat, bowrider, cabin cruiser, center console, cuddy cabin, deck boat, pontoon boat, canopy/bimini top, wakeboard, inner tube. Do not include synonyms or extra cues.
output_structure.unapproved_observations_report: Briefly list visible but unapproved observations that might otherwise influence visual reasoning, such as curved windshield, passenger cabin structure, sleek hull profile, seating layout, passengers, wake, color, apparent activity, tow rope, water spray, fish on line, or context. These observations must not influence boat_type unless an approved identifier is visible.
output_structure.decision_rule: Use fishing_boat if approved fishing identifiers are visible: fishing rods, fish landing net, trolling motor, jon boat, bass boat, all-purpose fishing boat, bay or flats boat, aluminum fishing boat. Use recreational_boat only if no fishing identifier is visible and an approved recreational identifier is visible: bowrider, cabin cruiser, center console, cuddy cabin, deck boat, pontoon boat, canopy/bimini top, wakeboard, inner tube. If both fishing and recreational approved identifiers are visible, return fishing_boat and mention the conflict. If no approved identifiers are visible, return unknown.

manifest.description: Summarizes boat detections, registration OCR, partial registration candidates, cleaned full-image OCR text, watermark date/time, and a clear one-line result.
Cleans text outputs, accepts focused boat OCR registrations again, and avoids stitching distant detected text regions into a fake registration.
Flattens the structured boat classification response into simple spreadsheet-friendly string fields.

Extracts confirmed boat registration numbers from OCR text, accepting LLNNNLL and LLNNNNLL formats, avoiding stitched text from separate OCR regions, and collapsing competing OCR letter reads that share the same numeric core while preserving separate registrations with different numeric cores.
Formats final boat registration status and output line after optional retry OCR has been merged.
Validates optional occlusion-aware registration reconstruction and exposes review-safe CSV fields without guessing unsupported registrations.
Returns the confirmed registration when present, otherwise returns the best partial visible registration candidate for review-safe CSV output.
